overview: After 1.d4 f5 2.Nf3 Black plays 2...e5, offering a pawn. After 3.dxe5 Black plays ...Nc6 or ...d6 to regain material or build pressure, while White keeps the pawn with e4 or Nc3. Black gets quick development and open lines but not enough for the pawn against good play.

white_ideas.idea: Take on e5 and defend with Nc3 and e3
Return the pawn if needed for a safe position

black_ideas.idea: Attack the e5 pawn and the open d-file
Use the f-pawn to open lines

typical_structures.structure: White up a pawn with open d-file
Black f5 pawn weakening the king

character.notes: A pawn-down open game where Black has to play for tactics.

gambit.notes: White keeps the e5 pawn after 3.dxe5 without being forced to give it back.

approach.notes: Strong players hardly ever play it.

level.notes: Dubious so never a good repertoire choice.

character.reason: Black is a pawn down in an open position and must play for activity.

gambit.reason: Black offers the e5 pawn and White can keep it.

soundness.reason: Black has too little for the pawn.

structure.reason: Pawns come off the centre and the d-file opens.

plans.reason: Black seeks development for a pawn.
